title: Beside the babblers: learned Roman doctors who hold their Church's mind more carefully
source_text: VI. Sed praeter istos blaterones, et sophistas nullius inter suos authoritatis, fatendum est, in schola Pontificia multos esse viros doctos, qui magis considerate et exacte loquuntur, majoremque delectum argumentorum habent. Hi certe sententiam Ecclesiae Romanae accuratius tenent, et melius explicant, cautiusque defendunt. Ideoque priores isti vitilitigatores coercendi sunt quidem, et reprimendi, eorumque stultitia, et impietas merito a nostris coarguitur, et publice vapulat. Veruntamen, quum status alicujus controversiae cum Ecclesia Romana quaerendus et constituendus est, non putamus istorum nugis esse inhaerendum: sed inquirendum quid sentiant et doceant posteriores, qui apud suos pollent doctrina et authoritate.
pass_a_gloss: But besides those babblers and sophists of no authority among their own, it must be confessed that in the Pontifical school there are many learned men who speak more carefully and exactly, and have a better selection of arguments. These certainly hold the opinion of the Roman Church more accurately, and explain it better, and defend it more cautiously. And therefore those earlier quarrelsome wranglers are indeed to be checked and repressed, and their folly and impiety are deservedly refuted by our people and publicly scourged. Nevertheless, when the state of some controversy with the Roman Church is to be sought and established, we do not think we should cling to those men's trifles; but we should inquire what the latter think and teach — those who among their own people are strong in learning and authority.
pass_b_english: Besides those babblers and sophists who carry no weight even among their own, we must admit that the Pontifical school has many learned men. They speak more carefully and exactly, and they choose their arguments better. These hold the Roman Church's mind more accurately, explain it better, and defend it more cautiously.

So those earlier quarrelsome wranglers should indeed be checked and put down; our people rightly refute their folly and impiety and expose it in public. Still, when we seek and fix the real state of a controversy with the Roman Church, we should not cling to those men's trifles. We should ask what the later sort think and teach — the ones who stand strong among their own in learning and authority.

choices.why: Classical sneer-word for litigious triflers; keep the bite without slang.
